changes.author: TKCollective
changes.text:
Follow-up to the measurement table above.

tanilo-receipt-verify now refuses an Ed25519 public key A or signature R that is mixed-order (outside the prime-order subgroup but not small-order), with reasons mixed_order_key and mixed_order_r. This was introduced in 0.2.2; 0.2.3 corrects test fixtures and documentation, with no behavior change. This stricter acceptance policy rejects mixed-order A or R before library signature verification, regardless of which equation the backend uses; 0.2.1 left those subgroup checks to the library. It is not a fix for a forgery against 0.2.1.

changes.author: guidoalejo
changes.text:
@stillmarcus24 - thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: there is no GMV or settled-call number to name, because the settlement metadata field is already live. You do not need to wait on volume to use it.

Once you claim the key and accept the rail terms dated 2026-10-14, `POST /facilitator/settle` takes an optional `originAssertion` string (max 256; charset `[A-Za-z0-9+/=._:-]`). Sluzen logs it on the settlement record as blind passthrough - we do not verify Ed25519, do not call `/notary/verify`, do not co-certify delivery, and settle does not depend on your notary being up. last_comment.author: Fizzl13
last_comment.text:
We implemented the single-payment part of this draft (§6, §7) in presign-guard, a pre-sign check for agent payments:

- POST /v1/check takes an optional mandate next to an EIP-3009 signature and turns a payment outside it red before the agent signs (wrong payer/asset/recipient, over perPayment or cap, expired, bad issuer signature, nonce ≠ binding).
- presign-guard-wallet's mandatePayer() makes x402 payments with the §7 binding as the EIP-3009 nonce.
- JCS bytes, digest, signature and the EIP-3009/Permit2 binding values match authority-vectors.json byte for byte.

Not covered: cumulative spend
